subject: Deal structure: minimums, leftover token allocation, and rounding rules
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deal structure: minimums, leftover token allocation, and rounding rules

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick follow-up on the two things your procurement team asked us to clarify: how per-call minimums and rounding interact with high-frequency short calls, and what happens to unused pooled tokens at month-end. I attached an updated pricing sheet (redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.xlsx) that shows two packaging options we discussed.

To make sure we propose something that fits your usage profile, could you confirm two pieces: 1) the typical median context length for your bot calls (prompt + expected response) and 2) an estimate of average calls per user per day for the pilot (ballpark is fine).

A couple notes on the options in the sheet so you have context before procurement reviews it:
- Option A (Seat + Pool): monthly committed token pool attached to seats. Leftover tokens can either roll forward for one billing cycle or be auto-burned depending on the SKU.
- Option B (Elastic with Minimum): per-call metering with a 10-token minimum per call and monthly smoothing credit for microcalls. Rounding rules are shown in the appendix — by default we round to the nearest 10 tokens for calls under 60 tokens to avoid billing noise.

We want to avoid surprises on your invoice. If you prefer, we can propose a hybrid: per-call billing but aggregate all calls under 50 tokens and bill them as an amortized monthly batch to reduce rounding losses.

I've looped in Ben (sales engineering) to draft a sample invoice example based on the numbers you share.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Jordan Blake

Subject: Re: Deal structure: minimums, leftover token allocation, and rounding rules

Jordan, thanks — and thanks for the call.

Quick answers: median context length (prompt + response) is ~72 tokens, but we have a long tail — about 15% of calls hit >1,500 tokens during document summaries. Average calls per active user/day for the pilot is roughly 18. Procurement asked specifically whether small helper calls (status, help, confirmations) will always round up to the 10-token minimum — those calls are frequent and would be ~6 tokens on average.

If we do a seat + pool, leftover roll-forward for one month would be preferred — we expect usage ramp and don't want to lose credits early. On the per-call model, procurement is worried about rounding inflation for the helper calls.

Can you send a sample invoice mock that shows: pilot month with 20 seats, anticipated call mix, and the two packaging options side-by-side? Also copy legal on the SOW changes.

Best,
Alicia
Head of Product — Acme Health
a.gomez@acmehealth.com

Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Deal structure: minimums, leftover token allocation, and rounding rules

Jordan/Naomi — forwarding Acme's note. Two quick thoughts before we send a mock invoice: 1) We should avoid an absolute 10-token minimum on helper calls unless we offer a monthly micro-call credit — otherwise their effective cost per helper call will be inflated. 2) For long-tail document summaries, suggest we map those to a separate SKU (long-context) that uses 1/4 token granularity and a separate bucket so they don't consume the short-call pool.

Proposed internal approach for the mock:
- Seat + Pool (preferred by customer): 20 seats, 1.2M token monthly pool, leftover rolls forward 1 month, long-context consumed out of a separate 500k long-context reserve billed at a lower per-token rate (quantized differently). Show sample invoice lines: committed pool, long-context pool, microcall adjustments.
- Elastic per-call: per-token pricing with a microcall smoothing credit: aggregate all calls <12 tokens daily, sum tokens, and bill daily in 10-token increments with a monthly negative smoothing credit if rounding overcharged them.

Naomi — can you draft the sample invoice lines and compute an example with Alicia's counts? If you need the distribution, assume 70% helper (6 tokens), 25% standard (72 tokens), 5% long-summary (avg 1,800 tokens).

- Ben

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Procurement <procure@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 13:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deal structure: minimums, leftover token allocation, and rounding rules

Alicia — thanks for the breakdown, that distribution is really helpful. Attached is a short mock invoice and two line-item examples (pilot_invoice_mock.pdf attached in the SOW package). Summary of the ask and our compromise proposal below: 

1) Helper/micro calls (~6 tokens)
- Compromise: we will not apply a strict 10-token floor. Instead, we'll aggregate micro calls (<12 tokens) per-day and bill the aggregate in 5-token increments, with a monthly smoothing credit if the daily rounding causes >5% overcharge relative to raw token usage. That preserves predictable billing but reduces unit inflation you were worried about.

2) Long-tail summaries
- We'll allocate a separate Long-Context reserve (500k tokens) billed at a long-context rate (lower $/token but measured at 0.25-token granularity for billing) so those don't cannibalize short-call pool.

3) Leftover tokens
- For the committed pool SKU: leftovers roll forward for one billing cycle. If you convert to a larger commit within 3 months, we'll retroactively apportion leftover credits to the new pool pro rata.

4) Auditability and invoice examples
- Attached sample invoice shows computed lines: committed pool, long-context reserve, daily microcall aggregation (with an example daily rollup and monthly smoothing line), and a final net credit.

If this sounds OK, procurement/legal can ask us to add a short MSA exhibit: "Billing smoothing and microcall aggregation" with the exact thresholds. We can provide the exhibit language for the SOW.

Next steps: procurement — confirm you want the roll-forward + 1-month policy and whether the daily aggregation buckets are acceptable; legal — if you'd like the exhibit language I can draft and push it to DocuSign for signature.

Jordan Blake
